root_cause.sentence: The first line to fail was the North Fort Myers 6 transformer, at 141% of its rating. Without the data center it would carry 76%: the new load pushed it over.

hospitals.assumption: A hospital counts as on backup power when the substation nearest it in the synthetic model lost at least 60% of its load. Real hospitals have their own feeders, generators and priority restoration.

cost.who_pays: under 1 cent to 4 cents per household per month (illustrative)

assumptions.note: How long the lost load stays dark (estimated from the incident's size, a rule of thumb).
1,503 MW of customers dark for about 22.3 hours (estimated from the incident's size) at LBNL's value of lost load by customer class, weighted by U.S. sales (2024 dollars).
The upgrades that stop the cascade, priced by voltage class and length: reconductoring to a new line (Black & Veatch, 2014 dollars raised to 2024); transformers at $7,250 to $13,450 per MVA.
The campus draws 50% to 80% of its size on average (LBNL) at Florida's 2024 average industrial price, 8.50 cents per kWh (EIA).
Illustrative: the upgrades paid back over 40 years at 7% a year, spread over the state's households; low, households pay their share of sales; high, all of it. Who really pays is up to regulators.

en.text: On a summer afternoon, a new 1,500 megawatt data center connects to the grid at Fort Myers. The grid there can take about 557 megawatts before a line overloads. Over nine steps, overloaded lines trip one after another, and about 784,000 people lose power.

es.text: En una tarde de verano, un nuevo centro de datos de 1500 megavatios se conecta a la red en Fort Myers. La red allí admite unos 557 megavatios antes de que una línea se sobrecargue. En nueve pasos, las líneas sobrecargadas se disparan una tras otra, y unas 784 mil personas se quedan sin luz.

en.text: Here is how the failure spread. When the North Fort Myers 6 transformer trips, its power shifts onto the Fort Myers 12 to Bowling Green 7 line, which climbs to 154 percent. Each trip does the same to the next line, until the grid gives way.

The North Fort Myers 6 transformer trips at 141 percent. The North Fort Myers 5 to North Fort Myers 6 line trips at 289 percent. The Fort Myers 5 to North Fort Myers 6 line trips at 213 percent. The Fort Myers 12 to Bowling Green 7 line trips at 211 percent. Steps five to nine: five more lines trip, and Naples and Fort Myers lose power.

es.text: Así se propagó la falla. Cuando el transformador de North Fort Myers 6 se dispara, su energía pasa a la línea de Fort Myers 12 a Bowling Green 7, que sube al 154 por ciento. Cada disparo hace lo mismo con la siguiente línea, hasta que la red cede.

El transformador de North Fort Myers 6 se dispara al 141 por ciento. La línea de North Fort Myers 5 a North Fort Myers 6 se dispara al 289 por ciento. La línea de Fort Myers 5 a North Fort Myers 6 se dispara al 213 por ciento. La línea de Fort Myers 12 a Bowling Green 7 se dispara al 211 por ciento. Pasos cinco a nueve: se disparan cinco líneas más, y Naples y Fort Myers se quedan sin luz. Luego la red se estabiliza, partida en pedazos.

en.text: How to fix it. If you want to build 1,500 megawatts here at Fort Myers, this is what you have to do. There is more than one way, and the engine re-ran every one.
Option one: upgrade one line and one transformer. It keeps all 1,500 megawatts. It costs an estimated $64 million. With it, no line trips.

Option two: aggressive Local Transformer and Corridor Reinfo (4 lines and 1 transformer, +2,666 megavolt-amperes). It keeps all 1,500 megawatts. It costs an estimated $213 million. With it, no line trips. The AI proposed this one, and the engine checked it.

Option three: maximum Capacity Expansion with Full Build (3 lines and 2 transformers, +3,404 megavolt-amperes). It keeps all 1,500 megawatts. It costs an estimated $108 million. With it, no line trips. The AI proposed this one, and the engine checked it.

Option four: balanced Multi Path Upgrade with Minor Curtailme (4 lines and 1 transformer, +1,847 megavolt-amperes). It keeps 1,470 megawatts of the 1,500. It costs an estimated $80.2 million. With it, no line trips. The AI proposed this one, and the engine checked it.

es.text: Cómo evitarlo. Si quieres construir 1500 megavatios aquí, en Fort Myers, esto es lo que tienes que hacer. Hay más de una manera, y el motor probó cada una.
Opción uno: reforzar una línea y un transformador. Conserva los 1500 megavatios completos. Cuesta unos 64 millones de dólares, según la estimación. Con ella, ninguna línea se dispara.

Opción dos: otra solución. Conserva los 1500 megavatios completos. Cuesta unos 213 millones de dólares, según la estimación. Con ella, ninguna línea se dispara. La IA propuso esta, y el motor la comprobó.

Opción tres: otra solución. Conserva los 1500 megavatios completos. Cuesta unos 108 millones de dólares, según la estimación. Con ella, ninguna línea se dispara. La IA propuso esta, y el motor la comprobó.

Opción cuatro: otra solución. Conserva 1470 megavatios de los 1500. Cuesta unos 80.2 millones de dólares, según la estimación. Con ella, ninguna línea se dispara. La IA propuso esta, y el motor la comprobó.

root_cause.sentence: The storm cut 150 lines. The first line to overload afterwards was the Titusville 5 to Titusville 8 line, at 103% of its rating; the data center makes no difference to it. Without the data center, about the same number of people lose power: 2.1 million (estimate).

hospitals.assumption: A hospital counts as on backup power when the substation nearest it in the synthetic model lost at least 60% of its load. Real hospitals have their own feeders, generators and priority restoration.

cost.who_pays: under 1 cent to 1 cent per household per month (illustrative)

assumptions.note: How long the lost load stays dark (estimated from the incident's size, a rule of thumb).
4,028 MW of customers dark for about 35.1 hours (estimated from the incident's size) at LBNL's value of lost load by customer class, weighted by U.S. sales (2024 dollars).
The upgrades that stop the cascade, priced by voltage class and length: reconductoring to a new line (Black & Veatch, 2014 dollars raised to 2024); transformers at $7,250 to $13,450 per MVA.
The campus draws 50% to 80% of its size on average (LBNL) at Florida's 2024 average industrial price, 8.50 cents per kWh (EIA).
Illustrative: the upgrades paid back over 40 years at 7% a year, spread over the state's households; low, households pay their share of sales; high, all of it. Who really pays is up to regulators.

en.text: Here is how the damage spread. The storm cuts lines first, and the power they carried shifts onto the lines still standing.

First, the storm knocks out 150 lines, and Naples loses power. The Titusville 5 to Titusville 8 line trips at 103 percent. The Punta Gorda 2 to Punta Gorda 1 line trips at 103 percent. The North Port 6 to Englewood 5 line trips at 171 percent, and Port Charlotte loses power. The Cocoa 8 transformer trips at 100 percent. Steps five to six: two more lines trip.

es.text: Así se propagó el daño. La tormenta corta líneas primero, y la energía que llevaban pasa a las que siguen en pie.

Primero, la tormenta derriba 150 líneas, y Naples se queda sin luz. La línea de Titusville 5 a Titusville 8 se dispara al 103 por ciento. La línea de Punta Gorda 2 a Punta Gorda 1 se dispara al 103 por ciento. La línea de North Port 6 a Englewood 5 se dispara al 171 por ciento, y Port Charlotte se queda sin luz. El transformador de Cocoa 8 se dispara al 100 por ciento. Pasos cinco a seis: se disparan dos líneas más.

en.text: No fix exists for about 1.95 million people. Even with unlimited line ratings and no data center, they stay dark: the storm cut the lines that serve them. The best fix we ran, line upgrades, stops the cascade that follows, and nothing more. Only rebuilding brings them back.
Of about 2.1 million without power, about 1.95 million are cut off by the damage itself, about 151,000 by the cascade that follows, and none by the data center.

De unos 2.1 millones sin luz, unos 1.95 millones quedan aislados por el propio daño, unas 151 mil por la cascada posterior, y ninguna por el centro de datos.

en.text: How to recover. Repair order matters: the right lines first bring the most people back per repair. Hardening the 10 most important lines ahead of time would keep about 775,000 people connected.

First wave: rebuild 4 lines, 157 kilometers; about 701,000 people get power back. Second wave: rebuild 8 lines in all, 272 kilometers; about 817,000 people have power back. Third wave: rebuild 16 lines in all, 385 kilometers; about 980,000 people have power back.

Primera ola: reconstruir 4 líneas, 157 kilómetros; unas 701 mil personas recuperan la luz. Segunda ola: reconstruir 8 líneas en total, 272 kilómetros; unas 817 mil personas ya tienen luz. Tercera ola: reconstruir 16 líneas en total, 385 kilómetros; unas 980 mil personas ya tienen luz.
